newsitem.title: UK: UK watchdog tells cable firms to work together.
newsitem.headline: UK watchdog tells cable firms to work together.

text.p: Britain's telecommunications watchdog Oftel on Wednesday urged cable companies to work together to compete more effectively with firms dominant in telecommunications and broadcasting.

Director general of telecommunications Don Cruickshank, speaking at a cable communications conference in London, said, "Co-operating, if it strengthens the effectiveness of the cable brand, will serve to strengthen competition in the UK market."
But he said competition authorities had to be wary of alliances and joint ventures of companies already dominant in related markets.

"Alarm bells should begin to ring, at least softly, when those dominant in the old (markets) move into the new. The ringing should get louder when two or more, dominant in different parts, get together."

Cruickshank outlined competition problems that might arise in the new converged telecommunications and broadcasting market, saying he would want a liberalised market in consumer equipment such as television set-top boxes.
"Elsewhere in the telecommunications equipment market competition has delivered significant benefits in terms of price, quality and variety of equipment."

He said customers would want "hassle-free" choice of equipment, which would allow them to switch between network and service providers without unnecessary costs. "And, in particular, without having to throw away existing equipment and start again."

He expressed concern about the benefits to consumers of subsidies for set-top boxes. "If the box does require an apparent subsidy, it should be provided in such a way that does not stop customers switching between delivery systems and/or service providers without having to scrap their kit and start again."
